title: Intelligence Layer: store root, identities, surfaces and the loop
content:
# Where the governed store lives

`/mnt/d/intelligence-layer/AI_Platform/intelligence` - moved off the C: Codex workspace on 2026-09-20.
Gateway `http://127.0.0.1:8765`, loopback only, systemd user unit `intelligence-gateway.service`.

## Identities (experimental, source-visible tokens)

| identity | scopes |
|---|---|
| `local-hermes` | read:approved, read:governance-metadata |
| `local-hermes-writer` | + read:candidate, write:candidate, request:promotion, withdraw |
| `local-agent` | read:approved, write:candidate, request:promotion, withdraw |
| `local-qa` | read:candidate, validate:candidate |
| `local-human` | approve, deprecate, rollback, withdraw:any |

## Surfaces and tools

Two MCP surfaces, deliberately separate programs. Read adapter `server.py` exposes five read
tools - `search_approved`, `get_approved_artifact`, `get_governance_metadata`, `get_provenance`,
`get_governance_events` - and contains no write path at all. Write adapter `write_server.py`
exposes the same five plus `submit_candidate`, `request_promotion` and `withdraw_candidate`.

Neither surface has validate/approve/deprecate/supersede, and there is no HTTP approve endpoint.

## The loop, with tools

1. `hermes-skill-backflow.py --source ~/.hermes/skills/local/<name>` (dry run) then `--apply` -
   files a skill candidate as `local-agent`, after running the skill's own tests.
2. `intelligence-validate.py --kind skill --id <id>` (dry run) then `--apply` - QA re-runs the
   artifact's recorded tests from the governed copy and refuses to validate what fails.
3. `intelligence-approve.py --kind skill --id <id> --apply` - the human approves. Never automate.

Artifacts written through the MCP write surface instead follow: `submit_candidate` ->
validate -> `request_promotion` -> approve.

## Rules that decide most questions

- A candidate may not shadow a live id (`approved`/`stale`/`deprecated`); an `archived` id is
  reusable, because an archived record is inert.
- `withdraw_candidate` retracts an unpublished artifact. Nothing is deleted: the status becomes
  `archived` with the reason kept, and it leaves the reading surface. Allowed for the identity
  that filed it (read from the append-only audit log, not from a claimant-controlled field) or for
  the human.
- `verified: true` only ever comes from approval; the write surface forces it false.
- Ids are path segments in the store, so they must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}`.
- A status change moves the artifact's whole directory and rewrites its recorded test paths.

## Feedback

`qa/events.jsonl` carries metadata-only lifecycle events (id, kind, from/to status, actor, never
content) behind `GET /v1/events?since=<line-offset cursor>`, or the `get_governance_events` tool.
A monitor-gated cron job (`governance-feedback`, every 3h) pulls the increment and reports.
